imagine you're sitting on a branch near the top of a sequoia tree. you've climbed pretty high, & the view from where you're at is gorgeous.
sometimes you wish you could climb a bit higher and see the view from the top, although your branch could have kept anyone content.
until one day, looking upwards and lost in thought, you slip. and you try to grab onto that old branch but it cracks under your fingertips.
so you fall. and you watch that view slip out over the treeline and you realize how little you appreciated it, selfishly striving for higher
fall down, down, down that sequoia tree, hitting every. single. branch. on. the. way.
until the forest floor finally grants you a twisted sort of reprieve in laying there, bloody, battered, bruised.
stare up that sequoia and stare at that broken branch and miss its splendiferous sights. regrets don't mean anything.
and that, ladies and gentlemen, is mood atm :]

apathy is a drug: it’s a heavenly drug, it’s a hell of a drug. the feeling it brings you, it’s like meth. it’s power.
power & freedom, that’s the feeling it brings you. freedom to do anything, because nothing matters. “i. don’t. care.” is the lively chanting
it incites, inside. you could do anything, no strings attached to make you feel, make you feel anything, won’t you feel anything at all?
no. while we ride the high, we are infinite. infinitely indifferent, indifferent to pain, indifferent to consequence.
and consequently, the consequences of our actions befall us. and fated, you fall. because all drugs have side effects.
as the high crests and falls, look at the damage you've done to yourself under its corrupting will & influence. you were never free.
look at the damage you've done to others. so powerful, and yet time brings even ozymandias to his knees. now deal with the reality.
was it worth it? well under the high it certainly felt so. for a time being you felt nothing mattered and that meant freedom.
freedom from the strings of reality, not that they were cut, but in your mind the strings no longer exist. nothing to bind you down anymore.
no, everything is fine when you're on apathy. or meth, feeling clear as crystal. same delusional detachment. states of altered consciousness
drugs. say the word. every drug feels like magic while you're on it. look at the damage and laugh, it’s not happening now.
the damage, it would appear, is sometime later. it’s soon, it might be tomorrow, but that’s okay. tomorrow never comes.
so we take the meth. did i run my car dead into a telephone pole? well it seemed fine while the meth was deciding it was fine for me.
it’s just a pole, it’s just a car, it’s just a scratch through which my FUCKING INTESTINES are falling out, but who cares? it's whatever.
i’m invincible, ozymandias. the suffering means nothing to me, not when i'm feeling so apathetic. on meth but i've never touched a needle.
no, it’s after the high, after the damage, after the hospital visits, that the reality of the damage you did sets in. caught in the strings.
a puppet of the drug, now a puppet strung & bound to consequence, damned to pick up the pieces and feebly piece them back together.
after the high dies, it’s the fearful stares from your family that will haunt you, leave you sleepless wondering how you just didn't care.
it’s knowing that they'll never trust you again that cuts into your chest, not the stitches. side effects of the drug.
good things tend to come with a price. of apathy, have the fun first. then come back and pay for it later with penance and regret.

identity is when all things about you are mentally collated in a place, so that when someone asks e.g. "what are you good at" you can internally query "what am i good at" and a list of things you're good at is already collected and stored in your memory

when you have NO identity, that list is unpopulated, making you think that you're good at nothing. yet, there ARE things which, when you think about them, you're good at. they just don't come up under your brain query of "what am i good at" -- which is the identity you're missing

and like how "expand your definitions" is difficult when the expanse that things can be expanded into is, obviously, unknown to you, it is hard to start thinking of things you're good at when we just covered that your brain does not have an answer to "what am i good at"

this is what makes it so tricky to develop! you basically need to wait around until you have spontaneous moments of remembering things you're good at and immediately write them down in a collected list, until you finally have something substantial which is usable as your identity

this WILL happen to you. like how you sometimes get a random burst of motivation at 3am -- you will randomly realize/remember things about yourself by chance and environmental entropy. the important thing then is to write them down as you remember.

this process is one from the same folder as e.g. "how do i get motivation to do stuff when i have no motivation," or "how do i be remember to be present in the moment when i'm not present" -- kind of chicken and egg problems that unfotunately mostly require waiting around.
but once you get going, solutions accrete on themselves (snowball/pygamlion/matthew effect). a little identity starts you on the way to building a lot of identity 🧶

gonna try to live tweet this out, but a thing happens to me from time to time when my subconcious has alarm bells ringing about the direction it thinks my life is heading in

it's something like this: when my subconscious withdraws its consent from what my conscious self is doing, it tries increasingly drastic effects to try to communicate this to me:

starting with

1) symbols and dreams
2) general feelings that something's wrong
3) revoking my ability to do things in that direction
4) actively trying to harm me

the last one is the most interesting

i read this phrase in "strangers to ourselves" by rachel aviv, the idea of a "slow suicide" unplanned; not consciously trying to die but your subconscious increasingly trying to make it more and more likely until statistics win. that's how it does it.

the last time i felt like this i lived in las vegas and i was horribly depressed. i went to work and all, and came back, and made good money, and by all measures should've been happy, but i just wasn't.

i had few friends in vegas and couldn't shake the feeling that i was wasting my life going to work and coming back. my subconscious withdrew its consent and i started showing up late to work. then, driving faster and faster there and back.

i got into street racing (lol). i would regularly drive 110-120 mph, not really intentionally, just on a feeling that none of this mattered and i wanted to feel alive somehow. what this really was i realized later,
was my subconscious saying "if you're not gonna listen to me i have no issues taking the both of us out." lmao.

now i'm here again and it's worse because then it was easy to point to what was wrong (my job sucked and i hated living in vegas). i since moved to LA and while i do still want to change jobs i have friends here and like LA. but it's back and i don't know why.

...
